info.bio: Cracker is an American alternative rock band fronted by Camper Van Beethoven singer David Lowery, with guitarist Johnny Hickman. They are best known for their hit songs "Low" and "Teen Angst (What the World Needs Now)". The band's website once noted Cracker as "The only band to ever open for both Grateful Dead and Ramones," a unique distinction which is also indicative of the band's sound and style. scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La revolución iniciada en Chicago por Souled American y Uncle Tupelo (No Depression: baladas country con la furia del hardcore) se convierte en los noventa en un género propio: sus herederos abandonan el hardcore por los sonidos más espartanos y tradicionales. Son Volt de Jay Farrar y Wilco de Jeff Tweedy (Being There, Yankee Hotel Foxtrot); Will Oldham (Palace) arranca el movimiento; Freakwater, Ida, Handsome Family, Retsin, Blue Mountain, Whiskeytown, Grant Lee Buffalo, Citizens' Utilities, Willard Grant Conspiracy. El «chamber folk» de Lambchop, Lullaby For The Working Class, Geraldine Fibbers y Pinetop Seven; el country-rock de Volebeats, Ass Ponys, Sixteen Horsepower, Old 97's y los terroristas Grifters; el folk-rock de Swell, Counting Crows, Cracker, Cake, Hootie & The Blowfish; los Black Crowes; Belle And Sebastian, Arab Strap y los polacos Atman.

podcast.title: The Cable Guy Soundtrack Contribution (1996)
podcast.body: Cracker contributed to *The Cable Guy* soundtrack in 1996, an album associated with the "creepy Jim Carrey vehicle" film. The soundtrack also featured other artists like Silverchair, Jerry Cantrell of Alice in Chains, and Porno for Pyros. "Silver Chair Jerry Cantrell of Allyson Chains, Porno for Pyrrho's Cracker, and primitive radio gods ended up with a hit with standing outside a broken phone booth with money in my hand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Camper Van Beethoven Spin-off
podcast.body: Cracker is a spin-off group from Camper Van Beethoven, and they achieved significant alt-rock hits during the 1990s. "Campers still exist today as does their spin-off group Cracker. They had some big all-rock hits in the 90s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
